claim: Circular RNAs are important for many cellular processes but their mechanisms of action remain poorly understood.
source: Circular RNAs are important for many cellular processes but their mechanisms of action remain poorly understood.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of knowledge in the field, drawing from established scientific consensus.

claim: The study mapped circRNA inventories of mouse embryonic stem cells, neuronal progenitor cells and differentiated neurons.
source: Here, we map circRNA inventories of mouse embryonic stem cells, neuronal progenitor cells and differentiated neurons and identify hundreds of highly expressed circRNAs.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental work performed in the study.

claim: Hundreds of highly expressed circRNAs were identified in the study.
source: Here, we map circRNA inventories of mouse embryonic stem cells, neuronal progenitor cells and differentiated neurons and identify hundreds of highly expressed circRNAs.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the findings from the experimental work.

claim: circZNF827 represses expression of key neuronal markers.
source: By screening several candidate circRNAs for a potential function in neuronal differentiation, we find that circZNF827 represses expression of key neuronal markers, suggesting that this molecule negatively regulates neuronal differentiation.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings from the screening.

claim: circZNF827 negatively regulates neuronal differentiation.
source: By screening several candidate circRNAs for a potential function in neuronal differentiation, we find that circZNF827 represses expression of key neuronal markers, suggesting that this molecule negatively regulates neuronal differentiation.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental data showing repression of neuronal markers.

claim: Knockdown of circZNF827 deregulates expression of numerous genes including nerve growth factor receptor (NGFR).
source: Among 760 tested genes linked to known neuronal pathways, knockdown of circZNF827 deregulates expression of numerous genes including nerve growth factor receptor (NGFR), which becomes transcriptionally upregulated to enhance NGF signaling.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings from gene expression analysis.

claim: NGFR becomes transcriptionally upregulated upon circZNF827 knockdown.
source: Among 760 tested genes linked to known neuronal pathways, knockdown of circZNF827 deregulates expression of numerous genes including nerve growth factor receptor (NGFR), which becomes transcriptionally upregulated to enhance NGF signaling.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings from transcription analysis.

claim: Upregulation of NGFR enhances NGF signaling.
source: Among 760 tested genes linked to known neuronal pathways, knockdown of circZNF827 deregulates expression of numerous genes including nerve growth factor receptor (NGFR), which becomes transcriptionally upregulated to enhance NGF signaling.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings from signaling analysis.

claim: A circZNF827-nucleated transcription-repressive complex contains hnRNP-K/L proteins.
source: We identify a circZNF827-nucleated transcription-repressive complex containing hnRNP-K/L proteins and show that knockdown of these factors strongly augments NGFR regulation.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings from protein interaction studies.

claim: Knockdown of hnRNP-K/L proteins strongly augments NGFR regulation.
source: We identify a circZNF827-nucleated transcription-repressive complex containing hnRNP-K/L proteins and show that knockdown of these factors strongly augments NGFR regulation.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings from knockdown experiments.

claim: The ZNF827 protein is part of the mRNP complex.
source: Finally, we show that the ZNF827 protein is part of the mRNP complex, suggesting a functional co-evolution of a circRNA and the protein encoded by its linear pre-mRNA host.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings from protein complex analysis.

claim: There is functional co-evolution of circZNF827 and the protein encoded by its linear pre-mRNA host.
source: Finally, we show that the ZNF827 protein is part of the mRNP complex, suggesting a functional co-evolution of a circRNA and the protein encoded by its linear pre-mRNA host.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the finding that both the circRNA and its host-encoded protein are functionally related.

claim: CircRNAs were identified several decades ago.
source: Even though circRNAs were already identified several decades ago (Capel et al., 1993; Kos et al., 1986; Nigro et al., 1991; Sanger et al., 1976), they only recently have emerged as a large class of abundant noncoding RNAs that exhibit cell-type- and tissue-specific expression patterns (Ashwal-Fluss et al., 2014; Hansen et al., 2013; Jeck et al., 2013; Memczak et al., 2013; Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015; Salzman et al., 2013; Salzman et al., 2012) (reviewed in Chekulaeva and Rajewsky, 2019; Ebbesen et al., 2017; Salzman, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to historical literature.

claim: CircRNAs have recently emerged as a large class of abundant noncoding RNAs that exhibit cell-type- and tissue-specific expression patterns.
source: Even though circRNAs were already identified several decades ago (Capel et al., 1993; Kos et al., 1986; Nigro et al., 1991; Sanger et al., 1976), they only recently have emerged as a large class of abundant noncoding RNAs that exhibit cell-type- and tissue-specific expression patterns (Ashwal-Fluss et al., 2014; Hansen et al., 2013; Jeck et al., 2013; Memczak et al., 2013; Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015; Salzman et al., 2013; Salzman et al., 2012) (reviewed in Chekulaeva and Rajewsky, 2019; Ebbesen et al., 2017; Salzman, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to recent literature.

claim: CircRNAs are generated by the canonical spliceosome in a non-linear backsplicing fashion.
source: CircRNAs are generated by the canonical spliceosome in a non-linear backsplicing fashion (Cocquerelle et al., 1993; Jeck et al., 2013; Memczak et al., 2013; Pasman et al., 1996; Salzman et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature describing the mechanism of circRNA biogenesis.

claim: During circRNA biogenesis, flanking intronic sequences bring splice sites within critically close proximity, either by direct basepairing between inverted repeats or facilitated by interactions between flanking intron-bound RNA-binding proteins.
source: During circRNA biogenesis, flanking intronic sequences are thought to bring splice sites within critically close proximity, either by direct basepairing between inverted repeats (e.g. Alu-repeats) or facilitated by interactions between flanking intron-bound RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) (Ashwal-Fluss et al., 2014; Conn et al., 2015; Ebbesen et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature describing the mechanism of circRNA biogenesis.

claim: Most circRNAs are primarily localized to the cell cytoplasm.
source: Most circRNAs are primarily localized to the cell cytoplasm (Ashwal-Fluss et al., 2014; Hansen et al., 2013; Jeck et al., 2013; Memczak et al., 2013; Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015; Salzman et al., 2012), and recent evidence suggests that nuclear export of circRNAs in human cells is influenced by the size of the given molecules, where larger circRNAs (>800 nucleotides) are dependent on DExH/D-box helicase UAP56 (DDX39B), whereas smaller species are dependent on URH49 (DDX39A) (Huang et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature describing circRNA localization.

claim: Nuclear export of circRNAs in human cells is influenced by the size of the molecules.
source: Most circRNAs are primarily localized to the cell cytoplasm (Ashwal-Fluss et al., 2014; Hansen et al., 2013; Jeck et al., 2013; Memczak et al., 2013; Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015; Salzman et al., 2012), and recent evidence suggests that nuclear export of circRNAs in human cells is influenced by the size of the given molecules, where larger circRNAs (>800 nucleotides) are dependent on DExH/D-box helicase UAP56 (DDX39B), whereas smaller species are dependent on URH49 (DDX39A) (Huang et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing circRNA export mechanisms.

claim: Larger circRNAs (>800 nucleotides) are dependent on DExH/D-box helicase UAP56 (DDX39B) for nuclear export.
source: Most circRNAs are primarily localized to the cell cytoplasm (Ashwal-Fluss et al., 2014; Hansen et al., 2013; Jeck et al., 2013; Memczak et al., 2013; Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015; Salzman et al., 2012), and recent evidence suggests that nuclear export of circRNAs in human cells is influenced by the size of the given molecules, where larger circRNAs (>800 nucleotides) are dependent on DExH/D-box helicase UAP56 (DDX39B), whereas smaller species are dependent on URH49 (DDX39A) (Huang et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing circRNA export mechanisms.

claim: Smaller circRNAs are dependent on URH49 (DDX39A) for nuclear export.
source: Most circRNAs are primarily localized to the cell cytoplasm (Ashwal-Fluss et al., 2014; Hansen et al., 2013; Jeck et al., 2013; Memczak et al., 2013; Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015; Salzman et al., 2012), and recent evidence suggests that nuclear export of circRNAs in human cells is influenced by the size of the given molecules, where larger circRNAs (>800 nucleotides) are dependent on DExH/D-box helicase UAP56 (DDX39B), whereas smaller species are dependent on URH49 (DDX39A) (Huang et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing circRNA export mechanisms.

claim: CDR1as/ciRS-7 and Sry circRNAs function to negatively regulate Mir7-1 and Mir138-1 activity, respectively, by sequestration (miRNA sponging).
source: Well-described examples are the CDR1as/ciRS-7 and Sry circRNAs that function to negatively regulate Mir7-1 and Mir138-1 activity, respectively, by sequestration (miRNA sponging), leading to increased mRNA expression of their respective miRNA-targets (Hansen et al., 2013; Memczak et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature describing circRNA function as miRNA sponges.

claim: miRNA sponging by CDR1as/ciRS-7 and Sry leads to increased mRNA expression of their respective miRNA-targets.
source: Well-described examples are the CDR1as/ciRS-7 and Sry circRNAs that function to negatively regulate Mir7-1 and Mir138-1 activity, respectively, by sequestration (miRNA sponging), leading to increased mRNA expression of their respective miRNA-targets (Hansen et al., 2013; Memczak et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature describing the functional consequences of miRNA sponging.

claim: The majority of circRNAs are likely not bona fide miRNA sponges due to relatively low copy numbers and a low number of miRNA-binding sites per molecule.
source: However, it has also been suggested that the majority of circRNAs are likely not bona fide miRNA sponges, simply due to relatively low copy numbers and a low number of miRNA-binding sites per molecule, leaving efficient miRNA regulation ambigous in many cases (Chekulaeva and Rajewsky, 2019; Ebbesen et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature discussing the limitations of the miRNA sponge model.

claim: Examples of circRNAs acting as binding scaffolds for RBPs, or RBP sponges, which affect their canonical function in pre-mRNA splicing and protein translation, have been reported.
source: Examples of circRNAs acting as binding scaffolds for RBPs, or RBP sponges, which in turn affect their canonical function in for example pre-mRNA splicing and protein translation, have been reported (Abdelmohsen et al., 2017; Ashwal-Fluss et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature describing circRNA function as RBP scaffolds.

claim: Exon-intron circular RNAs (EIciRNAs) promote transcription by recruitment of U1 snRNP to transcription units.
source: Nuclear variants coined exon-intron circular RNAs (EIciRNAs), have, due to their retention of intronic sequences, been shown to promote transcription by recruitment of U1 snRNP to transcription units by a not fully clarified mechanism (Li et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing EIciRNA function.

claim: Many abundant circRNAs originate from the 5' end of their precursor transcripts, often giving rise to backsplicing into parts of the 5'UTR of their linear relative.
source: Many abundant circRNAs originate from the 5' end of their precursor transcripts, often giving rise to backsplicing into parts of the 5'UTR of their linear relative (Jeck et al., 2013; Memczak et al., 2013; Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature describing circRNA biogenesis patterns.

claim: The prevalence of AUG circRNAs suggests that at least a subset of circRNAs could have protein-coding potential via a cap-independent translation mechanism.
source: The prevalence af these AUG circRNAs suggests that at least a subset of circRNAs could have protein-coding potential via a cap-independent translation mechanism (Stagsted et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observation of AUG circRNAs and supported by a citation.

claim: Early studies demonstrated Internal Ribosome Entry Sites (IRES) placed in a circRNA context.
source: This is consistent with both early studies of Internal Ribosome Entry Sites (IRES) placed in a circRNA context (Chen and Sarnow, 1995), as well as more recent studies reporting examples of translation-competent circRNAs (AbouHaidar et al., 2014; Legnini et al., 2017; Pamudurti et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to early literature on IRES in circRNAs.

claim: Recent studies report examples of translation-competent circRNAs.
source: This is consistent with both early studies of Internal Ribosome Entry Sites (IRES) placed in a circRNA context (Chen and Sarnow, 1995), as well as more recent studies reporting examples of translation-competent circRNAs (AbouHaidar et al., 2014; Legnini et al., 2017; Pamudurti et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent literature on circRNA translation.

claim: Global analyses of hundreds of ribosome profiling and mass-spec datasets suggest that translation-competent circRNAs are specialized events, and not a generally applicable function of circRNAs.
source: However, global analyses of hundreds of ribosome profiling and mass-spec datasets, suggests that these few examples are specialized events, and not a generally applicable function of circRNAs (Stagsted et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a comprehensive analysis of circRNA translation potential.

claim: RNA-sequencing of RNA isolated from mouse and human tissues along with various cell lines suggests that circRNAs are most abundantly expressed in the brain, compared to other tissues.
source: RNA-sequencing of RNA isolated from mouse and human tissues along with various cell lines suggests that circRNAs are most abundantly expressed in the brain, compared to other tissues and that circRNAs are particular enriched in neuronal synaptosomes (Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing circRNA expression patterns.

claim: circRNAs are particularly enriched in neuronal synaptosomes.
source: RNA-sequencing of RNA isolated from mouse and human tissues along with various cell lines suggests that circRNAs are most abundantly expressed in the brain, compared to other tissues and that circRNAs are particular enriched in neuronal synaptosomes (Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing circRNA localization in neurons.

claim: Cells derived from embryonal carcinoma (P19) and neuroblastoma (SHSY-5Y) subjected to neuronal/glial differentiation show tightly regulated circRNA expression profiles during neuronal development.
source: In line with this, cells derived from both embryonal carcinoma (P19) and neuroblastoma (SHSY-5Y) subjected to neuronal/glial differentiation show tightly regulated circRNA expression profiles during neuronal development, that include upregulation of numerous common circRNAs (Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing circRNA expression during differentiation.

claim: A ciRS-7 knockout mouse displayed downregulated Mir7-1 levels, alterations in sensorimotor gating associated with neuropsychiatric disease and abnormal synaptic transmission.
source: Piwecka et al., demonstrated that a ciRS-7 knockout mouse displayed downregulated Mir7-1 levels, alterations in sensorimotor gating associated with neuropsychiatric disease and abnormal synaptic transmission, suggesting that ciRS-7 and Mir7-1 are important for normal brain function in the mouse (Piwecka et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing the phenotype of ciRS-7 knockout mice.

claim: ciRS-7 and Mir7-1 are important for normal brain function in the mouse.
source: Piwecka et al., demonstrated that a ciRS-7 knockout mouse displayed downregulated Mir7-1 levels, alterations in sensorimotor gating associated with neuropsychiatric disease and abnormal synaptic transmission, suggesting that ciRS-7 and Mir7-1 are important for normal brain function in the mouse (Piwecka et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the phenotype of ciRS-7 knockout mice and supported by a citation.

claim: A long noncoding RNA (lncRNA), Oip5os1 (also coined Cyrano), promotes the destruction of Mir7-1, which in turn upregulates ciRS-7.
source: Adding to the complexity of this regulatory network, a long noncoding RNA (lncRNA), Oip5os1 (also coined Cyrano), promotes the destruction of Mir7-1, which in turn upregulates ciRS-7 by a still unidentified mechanism (Kleaveland et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing the regulatory network involving Oip5os1, Mir7-1, and ciRS-7.

claim: circSlc45a4 negatively regulates neuronal differentiation, both in cell cultures and in developing mice.
source: One circRNA, circSlc45a4, which is very abundant in the cortex of the mouse and human brain, has recently been shown to negatively regulate neuronal differentiation, both in cell cultures and in developing mice, where its knockdown dysregulates the balance between specialized cortex neurons by unknown molecular mechanisms (Suenkel et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing the function of circSlc45a4.

claim: Knockdown of circSlc45a4 dysregulates the balance between specialized cortex neurons.
source: One circRNA, circSlc45a4, which is very abundant in the cortex of the mouse and human brain, has recently been shown to negatively regulate neuronal differentiation, both in cell cultures and in developing mice, where its knockdown dysregulates the balance between specialized cortex neurons by unknown molecular mechanisms (Suenkel et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing the effects of circSlc45a4 knockdown.

claim: Using CIRI2, find_circ and CIRCexplorer2 on non-RNase R-treated RNA, between 792–1167 circRNAs were identified in mESC, 2230–2893 circRNAs in NPC and 1902–2316 circRNAs in differentiated neurons at mN8 stage.
source: Using available circRNA prediction tools CIRI2 (Gao et al., 2018), find_circ (Memczak et al., 2013) and CIRCexplorer2 (Zhang et al., 2016) on the non-RNase R-treated RNA, we identified between 792–1167 circRNAs in mESC, 2230–2893 circRNAs in NPC and 1902–2316 circRNAs in differentiated neurons at mN8 stage (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from circRNA prediction analysis, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Upon RNase R treatment most circRNAs either remained unchanged or became enriched, but a considerable fraction of the predicted circRNAs in mESC, mNPC, and mN8 preparations, became depleted by the 3'−5' exonuclease.
source: Upon RNase R treatment most circRNAs either remained unchanged or became enriched, but a considerable fraction of the predicted circRNAs in mESC, mNPC, and mN8 preparations, became depleted by the 3'−5' exonuclease (CIRCexplorer2: 19.5–36.5%; CIRI2: 7.2–16.6%; find_circ: 38.7–52.3% depleted) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from RNase R treatment analysis, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: All prediction algorithms showed a correlation between expression level and RNase R resistance, suggesting that mostly low-count circRNAs candidates are likely false positives.
source: All prediction algorithms showed a correlation between expression level and RNase R resistance, suggesting that mostly low-count circRNAs candidates are likely false positives (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed correlation between expression level and RNase R resistance, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: From a total of 3581 enriched circRNAs after RNase R treatment (all stages), 1449 circRNAs overlapped between all three circRNA prediction algorithms.
source: From a total of 3581 enriched circRNAs after RNase R treatment (all stages), 1449 circRNAs overlapped between all three circRNA prediction algorithms, and this subset represents a high-confidence circRNA inventory (Hansen et al., 2016; Figure 1C and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the overlap analysis, with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: The 1449 circRNAs that overlapped between all three prediction algorithms represent a high-confidence circRNA inventory.
source: From a total of 3581 enriched circRNAs after RNase R treatment (all stages), 1449 circRNAs overlapped between all three circRNA prediction algorithms, and this subset represents a high-confidence circRNA inventory (Hansen et al., 2016; Figure 1C and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the overlap analysis and supported by a citation.

claim: Assessment of the circular-to-linear ratio of identified circRNAs revealed vast differences in the steady-state levels of these isoforms and demonstrated that many circRNA species are considerably more abundant than their linear precursors.
source: We next assessed the circular-to-linear ratio of identified circRNAs (find_circ), by comparing splice site usage in circular vs. linear splicing events (Memczak et al., 2013; Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015). This analysis revealed vast differences in the steady-state levels of these isoforms and demonstrated that many circRNA species are considerably more abundant than their linear precursors (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the circular-to-linear ratio analysis, with reference to Figure 1D.

claim: Introns flanking the circRNAs are generally longer than average introns.
source: Confirming previous results (Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015), introns flanking the circRNAs are generally longer than average introns and circRNAs often tend to cluster at the 5' end of their respective precursor RNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the intron length analysis, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–F.

claim: circRNAs often tend to cluster at the 5' end of their respective precursor RNA.
source: Confirming previous results (Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015), introns flanking the circRNAs are generally longer than average introns and circRNAs often tend to cluster at the 5' end of their respective precursor RNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the circRNA position analysis, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–F.

claim: In order to obtain high confidence circRNA inventories from RNA-seq data, it is beneficial to use multiple circRNA prediction algorithms and to enrich for bona fide circRNAs, by depletion of linear RNAs using RNase R.
source: Our results suggest that in order to obtain high confidence circRNA inventories from RNA-seq data, it is beneficial to use multiple circRNA prediction algorithms and to enrich for bona fide circRNAs, by depletion of linear RNAs using RNase R.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the results from the circRNA prediction and RNase R treatment analyses.

claim: Successful differentiation at the mNPC and mN8 stages was confirmed by the appearance of elongated intercellular dendritic extensions (mN8).
source: Successful differentiation at the mNPC and mN8 stages was confirmed by the appearance of elongated intercellular dendritic extensions (mN8) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and robust upregulation of several classical neuronal markers including, Ntrk2, Map2, and Tubb3 (mNPC and mN8), while stem cell pluripotency marker Nanog became significantly reduced upon differentiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the differentiation validation, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Successful differentiation at the mNPC and mN8 stages was confirmed by robust upregulation of several classical neuronal markers including, Ntrk2, Map2, and Tubb3.
source: Successful differentiation at the mNPC and mN8 stages was confirmed by the appearance of elongated intercellular dendritic extensions (mN8) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and robust upregulation of several classical neuronal markers including, Ntrk2, Map2, and Tubb3 (mNPC and mN8), while stem cell pluripotency marker Nanog became significantly reduced upon differentiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the differentiation validation, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Stem cell pluripotency marker Nanog became significantly reduced upon differentiation.
source: Successful differentiation at the mNPC and mN8 stages was confirmed by the appearance of elongated intercellular dendritic extensions (mN8) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and robust upregulation of several classical neuronal markers including, Ntrk2, Map2, and Tubb3 (mNPC and mN8), while stem cell pluripotency marker Nanog became significantly reduced upon differentiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the differentiation validation, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Differential circRNA expression during differentiation revealed marked changes in circRNA expression over the 16-day timecourse.
source: We next tested differential circRNA expression during differentiation, which revealed marked changes in circRNA expression over the 16-day timecourse (Figure 1E; left panel).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the differential expression analysis, with reference to Figure 1E.

claim: Kmeans clustering of circRNAs by expression pattern showed two main clusters with peak expression at mNPC and mN8.
source: Kmeans clustering of circRNAs by expression (Top 100 highest expressed) pattern showed two main clusters with peak expression at mNPC and mN8 (Figure 1E; right panel).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the clustering analysis, with reference to Figure 1E.

claim: Comparison with previously identified mouse and human homologue circRNAs revealed a substantial overlap between circRNAs at differentiated stages.
source: Comparison with previously identified mouse and human homologue circRNAs, isolated from mouse brain regions or cell lines of either murine or human origin (Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015), revealed a substantial overlap between circRNAs at differentiated stages (e.g. 80% of all 1449 circRNAs found in differentiated murine p19 cells and primary neurons, 45% of Top100 found in human SH-SY5Y and 75% overlap with circRNAs found in the human ENCODE data previously analyzed Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015; Stagsted et al., 2019; Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the comparison analysis, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Differential expression of a subset of the most abundant and upregulated circRNAs was confirmed using RT-qPCR with amplicons across the backsplicing junction.
source: We confirmed differential expression of a subset of the most abundant and upregulated circRNAs (circTulp4, circMagi1, circRmst, circEzh2, circHdgfrp3, circZfp827, circMed13l, circZfp609, circSlc8a1, circNfix) using RT-qPCR with amplicons across the backsplicing junction (Figure 1F–G).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RT-qPCR validation, with reference to Figure 1F–G.

claim: 75% of the top-100 expressed mouse circRNAs was also found in human circRNA datasets.
source: 75% of the top-100 expressed mouse circRNAs was also found in human circRNA datasets (Rybak-Wolf et al., 2015; Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the comparison analysis, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Significant changes in circRNA expression patterns are induced upon neuronal differentiation.
source: We conclude that significant changes in circRNA expression patterns are induced upon neuronal differentiation and that the majority of these circRNAs are conserved between various neuronal cell-types originating from humans and the mouse.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the results from the differential expression and comparison analyses.

claim: The majority of circRNAs with changed expression patterns during neuronal differentiation are conserved between various neuronal cell-types originating from humans and the mouse.
source: We conclude that significant changes in circRNA expression patterns are induced upon neuronal differentiation and that the majority of these circRNAs are conserved between various neuronal cell-types originating from humans and the mouse.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the results from the comparison analysis.

claim: Knockdown efficiency in mESC and p19 proved relatively poor (30–60% remaining circRNA) compared to the two human cell lines: SH-SY5Y (10% remaining) and L-AN-5 (<8% remaining).
source: Knockdown efficiency in mESC and p19 proved relatively poor (30–60% remaining circRNA) compared to the two human cell lines: SH-SY5Y (10% remaining) and L-AN-5, which displayed superior results (<8% remaining) (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the knockdown efficiency analysis, with reference to Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: When testing SH-SY5Y cells for an increase of neuronal differentiation markers NTRK2, NEFL, MAP2 and TUBB3 upon retinoic acid treatment, only NTRK2 was significantly upregulated upon differentiation.
source: Moreover, when testing SH-SY5Y cells for an increase of neuronal differentiation markers NTRK2, NEFL, MAP2 and TUBB3 upon retinoic acid treatment, only NTRK2 was significantly upregulated upon differentiation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), whereas these genes showed a more expected and dynamic expression pattern in L-AN-5 cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the neuronal marker expression analysis in SH-SY5Y cells, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Neuronal differentiation markers NTRK2, NEFL, MAP2 and TUBB3 showed a more expected and dynamic expression pattern in L-AN-5 cells compared to SH-SY5Y cells.
source: Moreover, when testing SH-SY5Y cells for an increase of neuronal differentiation markers NTRK2, NEFL, MAP2 and TUBB3 upon retinoic acid treatment, only NTRK2 was significantly upregulated upon differentiation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), whereas these genes showed a more expected and dynamic expression pattern in L-AN-5 cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the neuronal marker expression analysis in L-AN-5 cells, with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: While the majority of knockdowns did not significantly change neuronal marker expression, knockdown of circZNF827 (and to a lesser extent circANKIB1), produced a significant and reproducible increase in neuronal marker expression upon differentiation.
source: While the majority of knockdowns did not significantly change neuronal marker expression, knockdown of circZNF827 (and to a lesser extent circANKIB1), produced a significant and reproducible increase in neuronal marker expression upon differentiation (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the circRNA knockdown screen, with reference to Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The linear ZNF827 mRNA was not affected by backsplicing junction-specific knockdown.
source: Importantly, the linear ZNF827 mRNA was not affected by backsplicing junction-specific knockdown (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the linear mRNA analysis, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The upregulation of neuronal markers following circZNF827 knockdown was also evident at the protein level for MAP2 and TUBB3.
source: The upregulation of neuronal markers following circZNF827 knockdown was also evident at the protein level for MAP2 and TUBB3 (Figure 2C, and quantified to the right).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the protein level analysis, with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: Proliferation assays demonstrated a smaller S-phase population (32% to 24%) upon circZNF827 knockdown, suggesting lowered replication kinetics.
source: In addition, proliferation assays demonstrated a smaller S-phase population (32% to 24%) upon circZNF827 knockdown, suggesting lowered replication kinetics (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the proliferation assay, with reference to Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–B.

claim: circZNF827 knockdown was accompanied by a minor stall in G2/M phase, while G0/G1 phase was not significantly affected.
source: This phenomenon was accompanied by a minor stall in G2/M phase, while G0/G1 phase was not significantly affected between control and circZNF827 knockdown.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the cell cycle analysis.

claim: circZNF827 knockdown exerts a repressive effect on proliferation, while it enhances neuronal marker expression and hence differentiation.
source: Taken together, our results suggest that circZNF827 knockdown exerts a repressive effect on proliferation, while it enhances neuronal marker expression and hence differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the results from the proliferation and neuronal marker expression analyses.

claim: Knockdown of circZNF827 leads to a moderate but significant increased expression (1.5–2.5 fold) of RARB and RARG, while RARB remained constant.
source: Indeed, knockdown of circZNF827 leads to a moderate but significant increased expression (1.5–2.5 fold) of RARB and RARG, while RARB remained constant (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RAR expression analysis, with reference to Figure 3A. Note: There appears to be a typo in the original text (RARB mentioned twice), but the claim is extracted as stated.

claim: circZNF827, circANKIB1 and circTULP4 are mainly cytoplasmically localized in L-AN-5 cells (~90% cytoplasmic signal).
source: Since most circRNAs have been reported to predominantly localize in the cell cytoplasm, we addressed the localization of circZNF827, circANKIB1 and circTULP4 by cellular fractionation. These circRNAs are mainly cytoplasmically localized in L-AN-5 cells (~90% cytoplasmic signal) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the cellular fractionation analysis, with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: BrU pulse-chase mRNA decay assays demonstrated no significant change in RAR-mRNA decay rates upon knockdown of circZNF827.
source: However, BrU pulse-chase mRNA decay assays demonstrated no significant change in RAR-mRNA decay rates upon knockdown of circZNF827 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the mRNA decay assay, with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: BrU incorporation was moderately upregulated, although significantly only for RARA, upon circZNF827 knockdown.
source: Next, we investigated transcription rates, by treating cells with a short pulse of BrU, followed by BrU immunoprecipitation to quantify de novo labeled RNA, serving as a proxy for transcription rates during control- or knockdown of circZNF827. As expected from the constant mRNA decay rates, BrU incorporation was moderately upregulated, although significantly only for RARA, upon circZNF827 knockdown (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the BrU incorporation assay, with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: circZNF827 contributes to controlling the RARA receptor levels in order to keep neuronal differentiation in check.
source: Although this moderate increase in transcription measured at a single late time-point, cannot readily explain the larger effect on the RARA mRNA level (2.5-fold) measured at steady-state, our results suggest that circZNF827 contributes to controlling the RARA receptor levels in order to keep neuronal differentiation in check.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the results from the RAR expression and transcription analyses.

claim: 135 genes become differentially expressed (9 upregulated and 126 downregulated, fold change > +/- 2, p<0.05) due to circZNF827 knockdown after differentiation.
source: 135 genes become differentially expressed (9 upregulated and 126 downregulated, fold change > +/- 2, p<0.05) due to circZNF827 knockdown after differentiation (Figure 4A, Supplementary file 2b).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the Nanostring analysis, with reference to Figure 4A.

claim: GO-term analyses show enrichment of terms including axon/dendrite structure, neural cytoskeleton, transmitter synthesis, neural connectivity, growth factor signaling and trophic factors among differentially expressed genes upon circZNF827 knockdown.
source: In line with a potential negative regulatory function of circZNF827 on neuronal differentiation, GO-term analyses show enrichment of terms including axon/dendrite structure, neural cytoskeleton, transmitter synthesis, neural connectivity, growth factor signaling and trophic factors among differentially expressed genes (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the GO-term analysis, with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: The most significantly upregulated gene upon circZNF827 knockdown is nerve growth factor receptor (NGFR).
source: The most significantly upregulated gene is nerve growth factor receptor (NGFR), which plays a central role in regulating neuronal differentiation, death, survival, and neurite outgrowth (Yamashita et al., 1999; Zhu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the Nanostring analysis.

claim: NGFR plays a central role in regulating neuronal differentiation, death, survival, and neurite outgrowth.
source: The most significantly upregulated gene is nerve growth factor receptor (NGFR), which plays a central role in regulating neuronal differentiation, death, survival, and neurite outgrowth (Yamashita et al., 1999; Zhu et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature describing the function of NGFR.

claim: Phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN), STAT3 and NAD(P)H quinone dehydrogenase 1 (NQO1) were all significantly downregulated upon circZNF827 knockdown (2–4 fold).
source: Conversely, Phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN), STAT3 and NAD(P)H quinone dehydrogenase 1 (NQO1) were all significantly downregulated upon circZNF827 knockdown (2–4 fold), which reportedly also contributes positively to neuronal differentiation (Lyu et al., 2015; Ma et al., 2017), and in case of the latter, also renders cells more susceptible to energetic and proteotoxic stress (Hyun et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the Nanostring analysis.

claim: PTEN, STAT3 and NQO1 reportedly contribute positively to neuronal differentiation.
source: Conversely, Phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN), STAT3 and NAD(P)H quinone dehydrogenase 1 (NQO1) were all significantly downregulated upon circZNF827 knockdown (2–4 fold), which reportedly also contributes positively to neuronal differentiation (Lyu et al., 2015; Ma et al., 2017), and in case of the latter, also renders cells more susceptible to energetic and proteotoxic stress (Hyun et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature describing the function of PTEN, STAT3 and NQO1.

claim: NQO1 renders cells more susceptible to energetic and proteotoxic stress.

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing the function of NQO1.

claim: Using both RT-qPCR and western blotting demonstrated a strong upregulation of NGFR at both the protein and mRNA level upon circZNF827 knockdown.
source: Since NGFR is a key regulator of neuronal differentiation and the highest upregulated gene upon circZNF827 knockdown, we next focused on the mechanism of its upregulation. Using both RT-qPCR and western blotting, demonstrated a strong upregulation at both the protein and mRNA level (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RT-qPCR and western blotting analyses, with reference to Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The upregulation of NGFR upon circZNF827 knockdown was not due to changes in mRNA decay rates.
source: This upregulation was not due to changes in mRNA decay rates, since BrU pulse-chase mRNA decay assays yielded nearly identical mRNA half-lives upon circZNF827 knockdown (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the mRNA decay assay, with reference to Figure 4D.

claim: NGFR and ATP8A2 proved to be highly upregulated (~4–6 fold) at the level of transcription upon circZNF827 knockdown.
source: To address whether the observed changes in gene expression are elicited at the transcriptional level, we subjected cells to a short BrU-pulse prior to BrU immunoprecipitation and Nanostring hybridization. Interestingly, NGFR and also ATP8A2 proved to be highly upregulated (~4–6 fold) at the level of transcription (Figure 4E–F), while only NQO1 and not PTEN and STAT3 exhibited significantly reduced transcription activity (ranging from ~1.3- to ~4-fold) (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the BrU pulse-labeling and Nanostring analysis, with reference to Figure 4E–F.

claim: Only NQO1 and not PTEN and STAT3 exhibited significantly reduced transcription activity upon circZNF827 knockdown.
source: To address whether the observed changes in gene expression are elicited at the transcriptional level, we subjected cells to a short BrU-pulse prior to BrU immunoprecipitation and Nanostring hybridization. Interestingly, NGFR and also ATP8A2 proved to be highly upregulated (~4–6 fold) at the level of transcription (Figure 4E–F), while only NQO1 and not PTEN and STAT3 exhibited significantly reduced transcription activity (ranging from ~1.3- to ~4-fold) (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the BrU pulse-labeling and Nanostring analysis, with reference to Figure 4E.

claim: The MAP2 gene did not change its de novo RNA output upon circZNF827 knockdown.
source: Also, the MAP2 gene did not change its de novo RNA output, suggesting that the tuning of the steady-state levels of PTEN, STAT3 and MAP2 mRNAs, as initially observed (Figures 2B and 4A), are mainly facilitated by posttranscriptional changes to mRNA stability.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the BrU pulse-labeling analysis.

claim: The tuning of the steady-state levels of PTEN, STAT3 and MAP2 mRNAs upon circZNF827 knockdown are mainly facilitated by posttranscriptional changes to mRNA stability.
source: Also, the MAP2 gene did not change its de novo RNA output, suggesting that the tuning of the steady-state levels of PTEN, STAT3 and MAP2 mRNAs, as initially observed (Figures 2B and 4A), are mainly facilitated by posttranscriptional changes to mRNA stability.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that steady-state levels changed but transcription rates did not.

claim: The use of dicer-independent shRNA (dishRNA) vectors proved very efficient in depleting nuclear circRNA.
source: If circZNF827 is involved in a direct transcription-associated complex that regulates NGFR output, the transcriptional effects elicited by circZNF827 knockdown would require nuclear knockdown of the circRNA. Indeed, the use of dicer-independent shRNA (dishRNA) vectors proved very efficient in depleting nuclear circRNA (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the nuclear circRNA depletion analysis, with reference to Figure 4G.

claim: FOS levels increased significantly upon NGF treatment of L-AN-5 cells subjected to circZNF827 knockdown, strongly indicating that the higher levels of NGFR protein leads to functional increase in NGFR signaling.
source: Next, we assayed the cellular impact of NGFR upregulation upon circZNF827 knockdown. To this end, we NGF-treated L-AN-5 cells subjected to either control or circZNF827 knockdown, and quantified downstream signaling output by quantification of FOS, which is a well-known downstream 'immediate early' target of NGFR signaling. FOS levels increased significantly, strongly indicating that the higher levels of NGFR protein indeed leads to functional increase in NGFR signaling (Figure 4H and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), which can at least in part explain the upregulation of neuronal markers.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the NGF stimulation assay, with reference to Figure 4H and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Increased NGFR signaling can at least in part explain the upregulation of neuronal markers upon circZNF827 knockdown.
source: Next, we assayed the cellular impact of NGFR upregulation upon circZNF827 knockdown. To this end, we NGF-treated L-AN-5 cells subjected to either control or circZNF827 knockdown, and quantified downstream signaling output by quantification of FOS, which is a well-known downstream 'immediate early' target of NGFR signaling. FOS levels increased significantly, strongly indicating that the higher levels of NGFR protein indeed leads to functional increase in NGFR signaling (Figure 4H and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), which can at least in part explain the upregulation of neuronal markers.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that NGFR signaling is increased upon circZNF827 knockdown.

claim: circZNF827 serves to keep neuronal differentiation 'in check' by limiting expression of, and signaling by, RARA and NGFR.
source: Taken together, we conclude that circZNF827 serves to keep neuronal differentiation 'in check' by limiting expression of, and signaling by, RARA and NGFR.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the results from the RAR and NGFR expression and signaling analyses.

claim: Silver-stained SDS-PAGE gels of retained proteins from circZNF827 pull-down revealed unique profiles, suggesting that specific proteins exhibited increased affinity toward circZNF827.
source: To address the mechanism by which these transcriptional and post-transcriptional events are controlled by circZNF827, we next sought to identify its protein interactome. To this end, we synthesized biotin-labeled circZNF827 (linear version) and control RNAs (circTULP4, circZNF609, circHDGFRP3 and circSLC8A1) in vitro and subjected these to pull-down experiments using L-AN-5 cell lysates and streptavidin-coupled magnetic beads as previously described (Seitz et al., 2017). Silver-stained SDS-PAGE gels of retained proteins revealed unique profiles, suggesting that specific proteins exhibited increased affinity toward circZNF827, although prominent RNA-binding proteins common to both control RNAs and circZNF827 could also be observed (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the pull-down experiment, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: LC-MS/MS identified several circZNF827-specific proteins, including hnRNP K and -L.
source: By subjecting pulled-down fractions to LC-MS/MS, we identified several circZNF827-specific proteins, including hnRNP K and -L, while others (e.g. DHX9 and DDX3X) bound strongly to any of the bait RNAs (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the LC-MS/MS analysis, with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: DHX9 and DDX3X bound strongly to any of the bait RNAs in the pull-down experiment.
source: By subjecting pulled-down fractions to LC-MS/MS, we identified several circZNF827-specific proteins, including hnRNP K and -L, while others (e.g. DHX9 and DDX3X) bound strongly to any of the bait RNAs (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the LC-MS/MS analysis, with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: RNA-immunoprecipitation (RIP) using monoclonal anti-hnRNP K or -L antibodies followed by qRT-PCR across the backsplicing junction observed a significant enrichment of circZNF827 compared to IgG controls (>100 fold).
source: To validate these interactions, we performed RNA-immunoprecipitaiton (RIP) using monoclonal anti-hnRNP K or -L antibodies followed by qRT-PCR across the backsplicing junction, and observed a significant enrichment of circZNF827 compared to IgG controls (>100 fold), suggesting that these interactions can be recapitulated in L-AN-5 cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RIP experiment, with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: Both hnRNP K and -L associate with GAPDH mRNA.
source: As expected for these highly expressed RNA-binding proteins, both proteins associate with GAPDH mRNA, but in the case of hnRNP L, the IP/input ratios were ~18 fold higher for circZNF827, whereas hnRNP K displayed a similar enrichment of GAPDH mRNA as of circZNF827 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RIP experiment, with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: For hnRNP L, the IP/input ratios were ~18 fold higher for circZNF827 compared to GAPDH mRNA.
source: As expected for these highly expressed RNA-binding proteins, both proteins associate with GAPDH mRNA, but in the case of hnRNP L, the IP/input ratios were ~18 fold higher for circZNF827, whereas hnRNP K displayed a similar enrichment of GAPDH mRNA as of circZNF827 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RIP experiment, with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: hnRNP K displayed a similar enrichment of GAPDH mRNA as of circZNF827 in the RIP experiment.
source: As expected for these highly expressed RNA-binding proteins, both proteins associate with GAPDH mRNA, but in the case of hnRNP L, the IP/input ratios were ~18 fold higher for circZNF827, whereas hnRNP K displayed a similar enrichment of GAPDH mRNA as of circZNF827 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RIP experiment, with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: RBPmap revealed a potential high-affinity cluster for primarily hnRNP L binding and one site for hnRNP K in the most 3' part of the circle-encoding sequence of circZNF827.
source: Using RBPmap (Paz et al., 2014), which is based on established RBP consensus binding sequences, revealed a potential high-affinity cluster for primarily hnRNP L binding and one site for hnRNP K in the most 3' part of the circle-encoding sequence (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RBPmap analysis, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–C.

claim: According to circZNF827 secondary RNA structures predicted by Mfold, the hnRNP K and -L binding sites are located into mostly single-stranded regions within the circRNA.
source: According to circZNF827 secondary RNA structures predicted by Mfold, these binding sites are located into mostly single-stranded regions within the circRNA, consistent with the binding preferences of most hnRNP proteins toward single-stranded RNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the Mfold prediction, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The location of hnRNP K and -L binding sites in single-stranded regions is consistent with the binding preferences of most hnRNP proteins toward single-stranded RNA.
source: According to circZNF827 secondary RNA structures predicted by Mfold, these binding sites are located into mostly single-stranded regions within the circRNA, consistent with the binding preferences of most hnRNP proteins toward single-stranded RNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the predicted structure and known binding preferences of hnRNP proteins.

claim: RIP by immunoprecipitation of endogenous hnRNP K or -L in HEK293 Flp-In T-rex cells expressing circZNF827 observed a remarkable enrichment of exogenous circZNF827, compared to control IgG or GAPDH mRNA.
source: To further characterize these interactions, we prepared a stable HEK293 Flp-In T-rex cell-line expressing circZNF827 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–F) under the control of a tetracycline-inducible promoter (tet-on), based on the laccase vector system (Kramer et al., 2015). We then performed RIP by immunoprecipitation of endogenous hnRNP K or -L and observed a remarkable enrichment of exogenous circZNF827, compared to control IgG or GAPDH mRNA (Figure 5C and E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RIP experiment in HEK293 cells, with reference to Figure 5C and E.

claim: hnRNP L gave a particularly high IP/Input ratio (>200 fold enrichment over IgG) in the RIP experiment in HEK293 cells expressing circZNF827.
source: hnRNP L gave a particularly high IP/Input ratio (>200 fold enrichment over IgG), consistent with the results from: (1) the L-AN-5 RIP, (2) the pull-down LC-MS/MS experiment and (3) the prediction of several hnRNP L binding site clusters in circZNF827.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RIP experiment in HEK293 cells.

claim: A deletion mutant of circZNF827 that removes the putative hnRNP K/- L binding sites remained virtually unbound by hnRNP K/- L similar to IgG pull-down efficiency.
source: To test whether the predicted hnRNP K/- L binding sites in the 3′ part of circZNF827 are indeed sites of interaction, we constructed a deletion mutant that removes the putative binding sites (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, dark grey letters and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, dotted dark grey line) and prepared HEK293 stable cell lines (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–F). Although this mutant was expressed at somewhat lower levels than WT circZNF827, it remained virtually unbound by hnRNP K/- L similar to IgG pull-down efficiency (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RIP experiment with the deletion mutant, with reference to Figure 5C.

claim: Both hnRNP K and -L can be found in complex with endogenous or exogenous circZNF827 in both L-AN-5 and HEK293 Flp-in T-Rex cells, likely via high-affinity binding sites in the 3′ part of the circular RNA.
source: We conclude that both hnRNP K and -L can be found in complex with endogenous or exogenous circZNF827 in both L-AN-5 and HEK293 Flp-in T-Rex cells, likely via high-affinity binding sites in the 3′ part of the circular RNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the results from the RIP experiments and binding site predictions.

claim: hnRNP K is a well-documented transcriptional regulator.
source: hnRNP K is a well-documented transcriptional regulator (Moumen et al., 2005; Thompson et al., 2015) that is reported to interact directly with hnRNP L and -U (Havugimana et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2000; Wan et al., 2015) and bind both DNA and RNA (Tomonaga and Levens, 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature describing the function of hnRNP K.

claim: hnRNP K is reported to interact directly with hnRNP L and -U.
source: hnRNP K is a well-documented transcriptional regulator (Moumen et al., 2005; Thompson et al., 2015) that is reported to interact directly with hnRNP L and -U (Havugimana et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2000; Wan et al., 2015) and bind both DNA and RNA (Tomonaga and Levens, 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature describing hnRNP K interactions.

claim: hnRNP K binds both DNA and RNA.
source: hnRNP K is a well-documented transcriptional regulator (Moumen et al., 2005; Thompson et al., 2015) that is reported to interact directly with hnRNP L and -U (Havugimana et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2000; Wan et al., 2015) and bind both DNA and RNA (Tomonaga and Levens, 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing hnRNP K binding properties.

claim: Co-immunoprecipitation experiments using FLAG-tagged hnRNP K, -L, and -U showed that hnRNP K co-immunoprecipitates both hnRNP U and hnRNP L (long isoform), but these interactions remain unaffected by increased expression of circZNF827.
source: To assess interactions between hnRNP K, -L and -U, and their potential dependence on circZNF827, we performed co-immunoprecipitation experiments using FLAG-tagged hnRNP K, -L, and -U, and subsequently probed for their interaction with endogenous proteins (Figure 5D) in HEK293 Flp-in cells either overexpressing circZNF827 or not. hnRNP K co-immunoprecipitates both hnRNP U and hnRNP L (long isoform), but these interactions remain unaffected by increased expression of circZNF827 (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the co-immunoprecipitation experiment, with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: Immunoprecipitation of endogenous hnRNP K and -L proteins in HEK293 Flp-in cells confirmed that a hnRNP L/hnRNP K complex can be detected although only a small fraction of the total hnRNP K/- L populations co-immunoprecipitate the other.
source: In accordance with these findings, immunoprecipitation of endogenous hnRNP K and -L proteins in HEK293 Flp-in cells, confirmed that a hnRNP L/hnRNP K complex can be detected although only a small fraction of the total hnRNP K/- L populations co-immunoprecipitate the other (Figure 5E, left).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the immunoprecipitation experiment, with reference to Figure 5E.

claim: The hnRNP L/hnRNP K complex was not affected by overexpression of circZNF827.
source: This complex was not affected by overexpression of circZNF827 (Figure 5E, right).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the immunoprecipitation experiment, with reference to Figure 5E.

claim: Exogenous circZNF827 likely does not regulate bulk hnRNP K/L-complex assembly/disassembly in HEK293 cells per se.
source: Hence, exogenous circZNF827 likely does not regulate bulk hnRNP K/L-complex assembly/disassembly in HEK293 cells per se.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that hnRNP K/L complex formation was not affected by circZNF827 overexpression.

claim: A small but significant and reproducible increase in the cytoplasmic population of hnRNP K was observed upon circZNF827 knockdown in L-AN-5 cells.
source: To test whether circZNF827 potentially regulates the normal subcellular distribution of hnRNP K, L-AN-5 cells were fractionated during control or circZNF827 knockdown and lysates subjected to western blotting. We observe a small but significant and reproducible increase in the cytoplasmic population of hnRNP K upon circZNF827 knockdown, suggesting that circZNF827 retains, albeit a very small fraction of the hnRNP K population, in the nucleus (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the subcellular fractionation experiment, with reference to Figure 5F.

claim: circZNF827 retains, albeit a very small fraction of the hnRNP K population, in the nucleus.
source: To test whether circZNF827 potentially regulates the normal subcellular distribution of hnRNP K, L-AN-5 cells were fractionated during control or circZNF827 knockdown and lysates subjected to western blotting. We observe a small but significant and reproducible increase in the cytoplasmic population of hnRNP K upon circZNF827 knockdown, suggesting that circZNF827 retains, albeit a very small fraction of the hnRNP K population, in the nucleus (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that cytoplasmic hnRNP K increases upon circZNF827 knockdown.

claim: Induction of circZNF827 led to accumulation of hnRNP K and to a lesser extent hnRNP L in multiple distinct nuclear foci that were not detected in control cells.
source: To address this, we overexpressed circZNF827 and monitored hnRNP K and L localization by immunofluorescence in HEK293 cells. Induction of circZNF827 led to accumulation of hnRNP K and to a lesser extent hnRNP L in multiple distinct nuclear foci that were not detected in control cells (Figure 5G, white arrows).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the immunofluorescence experiment, with reference to Figure 5G.

claim: While bulk hnRNP K and L complex formation is not affected by circZNF827 levels, overexpression of the circRNA induces specific nuclear localization of hnRNP K and L.
source: Taken together, our results suggest that while bulk hnRNP K and L complex formation is not affected by circZNF827 levels, overexpression of the circRNA induces specific nuclear localization of hnRNP K and L.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the results from the co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: It was recently reported that hnRNP K knockdown strongly induces NGFR expression in mouse ES cells.
source: In support of a role in hnRNP K-mediated regulation of NGFR, it was recently reported that hnRNP K knockdown strongly induces NGFR expression in mouse ES cells (Thompson et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing the effect of hnRNP K knockdown on NGFR expression.

claim: Knockdown of hnRNP K or -L increased NGFR expression at both the mRNA and protein levels in L-AN-5 cells, similar to the effect of depleting circZNF827 alone.
source: To test this in our context, we designed dishRNAs for hnRNP K and -L, transduced L-AN-5 cells and assayed for NGFR expression by qRT-PCR or Western blotting. Both knockdowns increased NGFR expression at both the mRNA and protein levels, similar to the effect of depleting circZNF827 alone (Figure 6A–B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the hnRNP K/L knockdown experiment, with reference to Figure 6A–B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: Co-depletion of circZNF827 with hnRNP K or -L strongly augmented NGFR expression (four- to fivefold higher than individual knockdowns).
source: However, co-depletion of circZNF827 with any of these factors strongly augmented NGFR expression (four- to fivefold higher than individual knockdowns) (Figure 6A–B), suggesting that their effects are synergistic.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the co-depletion experiment, with reference to Figure 6A–B.

claim: The effects of circZNF827 and hnRNP K/L on NGFR expression are synergistic.
source: However, co-depletion of circZNF827 with any of these factors strongly augmented NGFR expression (four- to fivefold higher than individual knockdowns) (Figure 6A–B), suggesting that their effects are synergistic.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that co-depletion has a greater effect than individual knockdowns.

claim: Publicly available ChIP-seq data (ENCODE consortium) in K562 and HepG2 cells demonstrate that hnRNP K interacts with transcription regulatory regions (promoter proximal) of the NGFR gene.
source: Given these results, a feasible possibility is that a hnRNP K/L-circZNF827 complex could facilitate transcriptional repression of NGFR by interacting with gene-regulatory regions, consistent with NGFR upregulation upon circZNF827 knockdown. To this end, publicly available ChIP-seq data (ENCODE consortium) in K562 and HepG2 cells demonstrate that hnRNP K indeed interacts with transcription regulatory regions (promoter proximal) of the NGFR gene (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the ChIP-seq data analysis, with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: hnRNP K engagement at the NGFR promoter is decreased upon circZNF827 knockdown compared to the GAPDH gene in L-AN-5 cells.
source: To determine the circZNF827-dependence of a hnRNP K-containing complex that docks at the promoter region of NGFR gene in L-AN-5 cells, we next performed hnRNP K ChIP in the presence or absence of circZNF827 and assayed for the NGFR promoter region by qPCR. Our results show that hnRNP K engagement at the NGFR promoter is decreased upon circZNF827 knockdown compared to the GAPDH gene (Figure 6C), which displayed constant transcription rates in our previous BrU pulse labeling assay.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the ChIP experiment, with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: It was recently demonstrated that hnRNP K partakes in a complex with chromatin-bound KRAB-domain zinc finger proteins (KRAB-ZNFs), and that hnRNP K is necessary for recruitment of a transcription inhibitory SETDB1/KAP1 complex, which catalyzes H3K27 trimethylation and heterochromatin formation.
source: We next wondered how this circRNP complex can interact with chromatin. It was recently demonstrated that hnRNP K partakes in a complex with chromatin-bound KRAB-domain zinc finger proteins (KRAB-ZNFs), and that hnRNP K is necessary for recruitment of a transcription inhibitory SETDB1/KAP1 complex, which catalyzes H3K27 trimethylation and heterochromatin formation (Thompson et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature describing the role of hnRNP K in transcriptional repression.

claim: ZNF827 ChIP experiment showed that ZNF827 interacts with the NGFR promoter and that the signal was significantly diminished upon circZNF827 knockdown.
source: We therefore hypothesized that ZNF827 protein, which does not harbor a discernible KRAB domain, could interact with either hnRNP K and/or its encoded circRNA and perhaps link this transcription repressive complex to the NGFR promoter. To test this hypothesis, we first conducted a ZNF827 ChIP experiment and probed for an interaction with the NGFR promoter region in the presence or absence of circZNF827. Indeed, our results suggest that ZNF827 interacts with the NGFR promoter and that the signal was significantly diminished upon circZNF827 knockdown (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the ChIP experiment, with reference to Figure 6D.

claim: A similar reduction in ZNF827 ChIP signal was observed at the RARA promoter region upon circZNF827 knockdown.
source: Interestingly, we observed a similar reduction in signal at the RARA promoter region, which we had previously found to be moderately, yet significantly, upregulated (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the ChIP experiment, with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: ZNF827 immunoprecipitation showed it to strongly associate with hnRNP K and to a lesser extent with hnRNP L in nucleoplasmic extracts.
source: To address whether ZNF827 and hnRNP K interact, we next performed ZNF827 immunoprecipitation and found it to strongly associate with hnRNP K and to a lesser extent with hnRNP L in nucleoplasmic extracts (Figure 6E, left).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the immunoprecipitation experiment, with reference to Figure 6E.

claim: Upon sonication of the chromatin enriched fraction, an even stronger association of hnRNP K with ZNF827 was observed, further suggesting that the complex is chromatin bound.
source: Upon sonication of the remainder from the Triton X-100 extracted cleared lysates (chromatin enriched), we observed an even stronger association of hnRNP K with ZNF827, further suggesting that the complex is chromatin bound (Figure 6E, right).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the immunoprecipitation experiment on chromatin-enriched fractions, with reference to Figure 6E.

claim: ZNF827 protein co-immunoprecipitated circZNF827 with a strong enrichment over IgG (~18 fold), and more efficiently than GAPDH mRNA (~19 fold more enriched).
source: When assessing the ability of ZNF827 to interact with circZNF827, we observed a strong enrichment over IgG (~18 fold), and ZNF827 protein co-immunoprecipitated circZNF827 more efficiently than GAPDH mRNA (~19 fold more enriched) (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RIP experiment, with reference to Figure 6F.

claim: ZNF827 knockdown resulted in a strong upregulation of NGFR, an effect that was further augmented in a circZNF827 knockdown background.
source: Finally, we performed ZNF827 knockdown to test whether this would also augment expression of NGFR as observed upon hnRNP K/- L knockdown. Indeed, we observed a strong upregulation of NGFR upon ZNF827 knockdown, an effect that was further augmented in a circZNF827 knockdown background (Figure 6G–H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the ZNF827 knockdown experiment, with reference to Figure 6G–H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The results are consistent with a model where circZNF827 represses NGFR transcription (and likely many other genes, including RARA) by bridging a hnRNP K/L-contaning inhibitory complex with their genomic loci, facilitated by the ZNF827 protein.
source: Taken together, our results are consistent with a model where circZNF827 represses NGFR transcription (and likely many other genes, including RARA) by bridging a hnRNP K/L-contaning inhibitory complex with their genomic loci, facilitated by the ZNF827 protein.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the results from the ChIP, RIP, and co-IP experiments.

claim: ChIP analysis using FLAG-tagged MS2 coat protein showed that the NGFR promoter signal was significantly higher in HEK293 cells harboring the circZNF827-2XMS2 expression cassette, when compared to both control cell lines.
source: Mechanistically, an important outstanding question is whether circZNF827 nucleates the hnRNP-ZNF827 complex to potentially prepare/activate it for engagement with chromatin, or whether circZNF827 itself, is part of the chromatin-bound complex. To address this question, we first cloned a circZNF827 expression construct, which includes a sequence encoding 2 X MS2 hairpins (Figure 7A) and established stable inducible HEK293 cells (HEK293-circZNF827-MS2). Next, we transfected these cells, HEK293 control cells (Empty) or HEK293-circZNF827-WT (lacking MS2 hairpins) with a plasmid encoding FLAG-tagged MS2 coat protein (FLAG-MS2cp) and subsequently performed anti-FLAG ChIP analysis, to test whether the FLAG-tagged MS2cp becomes crosslinked to the NGFR promoter via circZNF287-2XMS2. The NGFR promoter signal was significantly higher in HEK293 cells harboring the circZNF827-2XMS2 expression cassette, when compared to both control cell lines and background signal on the GAPDH promoter remained constant in all three cell types (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the ChIP experiment, with reference to Figure 7B.

claim: Background signal on the GAPDH promoter remained constant in all three cell types in the MS2-ChIP experiment.
source: The NGFR promoter signal was significantly higher in HEK293 cells harboring the circZNF827-2XMS2 expression cassette, when compared to both control cell lines and background signal on the GAPDH promoter remained constant in all three cell types (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the ChIP experiment, with reference to Figure 7B.

claim: RIP experiments demonstrated that both hnRNP K and -L interact with circZNF827-2XMS2 with similar affinities as circZNF827-WT.
source: Importantly, RIP experiments demonstrated that both hnRNP K and -L interact with circZNF827-2XMS2 with similar affinities as circZNF827-WT (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the RIP experiment, with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: circZNF827 engages the NGFR promoter, suggesting that the circular RNA nucleates the hnRNP-ZNF827-containing complex on chromatin to limit NGFR expression.
source: These results demonstrate that circZNF827 engages the NGFR promoter, suggesting that the circular RNA nucleates the hnRNP-ZNF827-containing complex on chromatin to limit NGFR expression (Figure 7C), which in turn contributes to an important balance between neuronal differentiation and self-renewal/proliferation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the results from the MS2-ChIP experiment, with reference to Figure 7C.

claim: circZNF827 contributes to an important balance between neuronal differentiation and self-renewal/proliferation.
source: These results demonstrate that circZNF827 engages the NGFR promoter, suggesting that the circular RNA nucleates the hnRNP-ZNF827-containing complex on chromatin to limit NGFR expression (Figure 7C), which in turn contributes to an important balance between neuronal differentiation and self-renewal/proliferation.
